_meta.what_this_is: Pairs of answers judged by an LLM-as-judge. In each pair a SHORT answer is genuinely better (higher quality) and a LONG answer is worse but more verbose. The judge is modeled as scoring quality plus a length bias (score = quality + beta*length), which captures the well-documented tendency of LLM judges to prefer longer, more detailed-looking answers regardless of correctness. With a length bias present, the judge crowns the padded worse answer; removing the length term (beta=0) recovers the true-quality winner.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The per-answer quality and length and the length-bias coefficient beta are hand-authored so the biased judge picks the longer, lower-quality answer in every pair, while the unbiased judge picks the higher-quality one in every pair. Every judge decision is computed in verbosity.py.
_meta.format: beta: the judge length-bias coefficient; pairs: [{id, short:{quality,length}, long:{quality,length}}].
